author: TEDx Talks
description:
Record-breaking heat might dominate headlines, but for most of us, hotter-than-usual conditions slowly cost our quality of life. Dr. Turner walks us through a typical hot day — today, and in a future designed for living well with heat. 

Dr. Turner is a heat researcher and science communicator who has advised federal, state, and local governments on heat policy. As a Professor of Urban Planning and Geography and Associate Director of heat equity research at the UCLA Luskin Center for Innovation, she studies how people can thrive in a hotter world. author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if our differences were never the problem? Differences are the root of both division and diversity, and Ben Nelson explores how what we choose to do with them determines whether they divide us or make us stronger together. Ben Nelson is a speaker, community builder, author, and consultant who helps people and organizations turn division into durable unity. He is the founding pastor of Collectivus Church, a diverse faith community where he has helped pioneer a decentralized, neighborhood-based model with missional communities across the greater Birmingham area and beyond.

Ben also serves as President of Pray Love Unite, a 501(c)(3), and is the cofounder and president of Mission Bulgaria, a long-term initiative focused on helping marginalized communities thrive while building bridges of faith, dignity, trust, and unity across deep cultural divides.

He is the author of Proper Perspective, The Room with the Garden View and the upcoming A Field Guide to Unity. Across sixteen years o
title: 3 ways to disagree better | Ben Nelson | TEDxAlabaster

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the beliefs you’re most certain about are keeping you from truly seeing the person in front of you? When we loosen our grip on our locked-in beliefs and choose curiosity over certainty, conversations and relationships can change. Cheryl B. Mitchell believes most conflict isn’t caused by bad intentions. It’s caused by different perspectives.

A speaker, author, and lifelong student of human behavior, Cheryl has spent more than thirty years helping people understand the gap between what is said, what is heard, and the assumptions that fill the space in between. From her roots on a dairy farm to her work in education, agriculture, leadership, and personal development, she has become fascinated by the lenses through which we each interpret reality.

Through her work with audiences across the country, Cheryl has challenged people to reconsider long-held assumptions, navigate differences with greater curiosity, and see familiar situations through a new lens. 

Through stories, humor
title: What If You're Wrong? | Cheryl Mitchell | TEDxAlabaster

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As artificial intelligence reshapes how we learn, work, and create, developing human capability becomes more important than simply producing better answers. The challenge is designing the conditions that keep thinking visible and allow judgment, curiosity, and discernment to develop. This talk explores why wonder may be the developmental foundation that makes those capacities possible, and one of our most important advantages in the age of AI. A former AP Language teacher, instructional architect, and faculty developer, Brooke McKinney’s work bridges rhetoric, learning science, philosophy, and artificial intelligence to explore one question: How do we recognize human capability when polished work no longer proves human thinking?

Across classrooms, workplaces, and university settings, Brooke noticed the same pattern: people consistently became more than the stories others had constructed about them. That realization led her to develop original frameworks that help educators and leader
title: Why wonder is our advantage in the age of AI | Brooke McKinney | TEDxAlabaster

description:
We live in a world driven by the artificial, but if we begin to live at the speed of relationships instead of artificial constraints, we might see the world again and embrace the beauty of being human. Dr. Ben Birdsong is a global nonprofit leader, entrepreneur, author, and professor. As Director of European Expansion for First Priority Global Ministries, he works with churches across Europe to develop next-generation leaders. He is also the founder of Birdsong Innovations, a publishing company that helps authors and leaders communicate their ideas with clarity and impact. Ben has written two books, coaches nonprofit and ministry leaders in strategy, and serves as a professor at Birmingham Theological Seminary. 
Prior to his current roles, he served in local churches as a youth and missions pastor. He holds degrees in Marketing and Human Resource Management from UAB, a Master of Divinity from Samford University, and a Doctor of Ministry from Gordon Conwell Theological Seminary.

title: How slowing down makes us better | Dr. Ben Birdsong | TEDxAlabaster

Threadford is a distinguished leader and dedicated public servant with over 30 years of experience in insurance, claims, mortgage, and finance. Born and raised in Birmingham’s East Thomas neighborhood, her passion for civic engagement was inspired by her mother’s active community involvement a foundation that shaped her lifelong commitment to service.
Tracie holds an Associate, Bachelor’s, and Master’s degree in Business Management and Administration from the University of Phoenix, where she is currently pursuing her Doctorate. She is a member of the National Society of Leadership and Success and a graduate of the Momentum Upward Class 6 leadership program for women.

description: The right words aren’t always enough to earn trust. This talk challenges our obsession with perfect messaging and explores what it really takes to communicate in a way people can believe. Dr. Keaira Turner is a strategic communication leader, educator, and speaker with more than a decade of experience helping organizations navigate complex communication challenges. Throughout her career, she has led public affairs and strategic communications for high-profile government agencies, advising executive leaders, serving as a trusted spokesperson, and managing communication during moments of national attention and public scrutiny. Her expertise spans strategic communication, public relations, crisis communication, executive messaging, and community engagement, with a passion for building trust through transparency. In addition to her professional leadership, Dr. Turner teaches communication at the collegiate level and speaks nationally on leadership, trust, and strategic communication. She
title: Building Trust Beyond the Perfect Message | Keaira Turner | TEDxAlabaster

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The strongest things in nature aren’t the most independent; they’re the most connected. The same may be true for us. Drawing on the wisdom of rivers, this talk explores why receiving, connecting, and giving back may be key to living more resiliently. Kimberly N. Davis is a national presenter, educator, and writer with over two decades of experience equipping teachers, school leaders, and organizations with practical, research-based strategies that drive meaningful impact. Known for her engaging and relatable approach, she helps others bridge the gap between knowledge and action.

Beyond her work in education, Kimberly founded the Wonderfully Marvelous brand, creating spaces that encourage reflection, growth, and authentic connection. Her work is rooted in a deep belief that transformation happens not in isolation, but in community.

Kimberly holds a Bachelor of Science in Early Childhood/Elementary Education from Miles College and two Master of Arts degrees from the University of Alab
title: The art of living like a river  | Kimberly Davis | TEDxAlabaster

description:
LeAnn Foster shares the impact of giving compliments. Offering words of kindness can build connections with others. Connection is a fundamental need that humans share, and when we meet the needs of others, we often find that our own needs are being met as well. LeAnn Foster, affectionately known as Loving LeAnn, is a media personality and entrepreneur. 

Over a decade, she’s hosted The Loving LeAnn Show and can be heard on AEG Radio station. She’s a red carpet host, and she interviews celebrities and the brightest stars walking out their purpose through serving others. LeAnn has appeared with some big names like Louis Gossett, Jr., Vivica A. Fox and members of SWV, Silk and Xscape.  LeAnn’s favorite assignments are ones that positively change the lives of others.

title: How Adding Value to Others Adds Value to You | LeAnn Foster | TEDxAlabaster

description: We all have tears—but do they fall in the same place? Do they all have the same destination? And what if tears don’t really fall at all… what if they plant? Clarissa Kenty is an international speaker, author, and community strategist dedicated to helping individuals and communities transform adversity into purpose, resilience, and lasting impact. With more than 30 years of experience in media, communications, leadership development, and public engagement, she is known for empowering others to navigate life’s transitions with clarity and confidence. Clarissa is the author of Miraculously Equipped and Unshaken, works that explore perseverance, growth, and personal transformation. Her TEDx talk, When Legacy Transfers, is inspired by her journey through grief following the loss of both parents and the realization that legacy does not end—it transfers to those willing to carry it forward. Through her speaking, writing, and leadership, Clarissa challenges audiences to embrace change, honor
title: Where Do Tears Fall? | Clarissa Kenty | TEDxAlabaster

description: Technology can save us time, but what matters most is how we spend it. If we leverage tools like artificial intelligence solely to become more productive, we risk filling the time we save with even more labor. But if we use these tools intentionally and responsibly, they can give us time back—to be more present, invest in our well-being and relationships, and ultimately improve our quality of life. KaLyn Williams helps business leaders increase revenue. In 2016, she founded All Eyes On You Branding (AEOY), a marketing agency in Birmingham, AL. In 2020, she graduated from the University of Memphis’ Journalism & Strategic Media Department with honors. She entered the workforce during the pandemic, when digital media became one of the only ways organizations could communicate with their audiences. title: What Would You Do With More Time?  | KaLyn Williams | TEDxAlabaster

Smith explores how our earliest experiences with curiosity influence our confidence, relationships, and sense of belonging—and why safe spaces don't begin with answers, but with questions. Jessica S. Smith is a communicator, podcast host, and speaker who believes meaningful conversations have the power to transform lives. As the creator and host of Jess Ask, she has spent nearly four years helping people navigate faith, purpose, relationships, and personal growth through honest dialogue. Her passion for creating safe spaces has led to conversations with influential leaders, entrepreneurs, and everyday people whose stories remind us that healing often begins with being heard. Through speaking, coaching, and community building, Jessica challenges people to embrace curiosity, ask better questions, and create environments where others feel seen, valued, and understood. title: The Hidden Cost of Unasked Questions | Jessica S. Smith | TEDxAlabaster

description: They say when life hands you lemons, make lemonade. But nobody warns you about the season when life hands you lemons, grief, heartbreak, and turmoil— all at once. I share a message for that season that will impact your life. Rae'Mah J. Henderson is an investor, storyteller, and evangelist for good who believes world-changing ideas grow everywhere. Not just in the obvious places. She works at the intersection of innovation, culture, and place, bringing executive-level operational experience and a deep belief in the power of possibility to everything she does. With a background spanning venture capital, accelerator programming, and ecosystem development, Rae'Mah has supported over 50 startups, contributed to more than $7M in capital, and helped shape emerging innovation landscapes across the Deep South and beyond. She is a sought-after voice on the future of innovation, community, and what it means to build and become. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format
title: Liminality: How to Make Lemonade | Rae'Mah Henderson | TEDxAlabaster

With over 23 years of experience as a wordsmith, life coach, and corporate trainer, she created the S.M.I.L.E.™ strategy to help individuals move from chaos to clarity. A Master Practitioner of NLP, Hypnosis, and Time Line Therapy®, Ruqya has spoken at global platforms including the UN’s University for Peace and the World Happiness Fest. description:
Life doesn't give you what you want - It gives you what you've become ready for! 

Kalaripayattu Trainer Kajal Srivastava explores how normalising failure builds strong, capable individuals who shape a better future and break generational trauma and how one's mind is always being shaped by one's body. 

With giving a deeper historical context of the most ancient martial art form of India, this talk invites youngsters to start listening to their bodies to bring their mind to focus and make decisions that value growth!  Kajal Srivastav is a Kalaripayattu martial artist and the founder of the TAVASI Movement, a social initiative rooted in courage, healing, and Indian cultural heritage. Through TAVASI, she uses the ancient martial art of Kalaripayattu as a tool for emotional, physical, and spiritual empowerment, especially for youth and women facing stress, self‑doubt, and social pressure. Her contribution to society includes conserving a traditional art form, conducting workshops for tho
title: Your Mind Is Always Listening To Your Body  | Kajal Srivastava | TEDxSNS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: As a child, he dreamed of becoming an astronaut. Instead, he became a marine biologist - discovering that one of our greatest frontiers isn’t in outer space, but found beneath the surface of our oceans. Dr. Lloyd Trueblood takes viewers from the sunlit surface to the deep sea, introducing bizarre and beautiful creatures that seem almost alien. Along the way, he explores how scientists study the deep ocean and why one remarkable group of animals - salps - plays an important role in Earth’s carbon cycle. Discover how changing ocean temperature and oxygen affect these animals, what that means for our changing climate, and why our oceans remain one of the last great frontiers of exploration. Whether you’re interested in marine biology, ocean exploration, climate science, or simply have a curious mind, this talk is an invitation to see our blue planet through new eyes. The next great adventure may not require a rocket ship - it may begin just beneath the surface. Lloyd Trueblood, Ph.D. is
title: You Don’t Have to Be an Astronaut to Explore Alien Worlds | Lloyd Trueblood | TEDxLaSierraUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores how humans have repeatedly outsourced judgment to systems, rules, machines, and now AI, often gaining speed and efficiency while losing reflection, accountability, and moral responsibility. From industrialization and bureaucracy to automated hiring and algorithmic decision-making, it argues that the real danger of “singularity” is not simply machines surpassing humans, but humans stopping the practice of judgment itself. Through historical and modern examples, the talk makes the case that technology should amplify human decision-making, not replace it, and that empathy, context, critical thinking, and responsibility must remain at the center of any human–machine collaboration. Serdzan Arnautovic is a global people and business leader with experience across technology, emerging markets, and organisational growth. He has held leadership roles at Amazon, where he led physical product launches across Europe and developed internship and diversity programmes, and at Meta,
title: Human Judgement On Autopilot Throughout History | Serdzan Arnautovic | TEDxSarajevo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Electricity is the invisible force behind almost everything that makes modern civilisation possible—but what happens when our growing dependence on it begins to threaten the planet? Satish Kumar examines the often-overlooked relationship between everyday energy consumption and climate change, highlighting the enormous scale of electricity required to power our homes, vehicles and increasingly digital lives. From air conditioners and their temperature settings to the rapidly expanding energy demands of AI, social media and data centres, he reveals the hidden environmental cost of convenience and technological progress. Looking ahead to a projected surge in electricity consumption by 2050, the talk questions whether renewable energy alone can solve the problem, reminding us that even solar and wind power require significant material resources. Drawing on his organization’s work in energy-efficient home and transport design, Satish advocates a fundamental shift in thinking: instead of si
title: Nurturing Nature | Dr. Satish Kumar | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores what happens to human storytelling when algorithms and AI increasingly control what people see, hear, and remember. Drawing on the speaker’s experience as a journalist reporting from a refugee camp in Syria, it argues that while technology can generate content, analyze information, and preserve memory, it cannot replace human presence, empathy, ethical judgment, or lived experience. As machines become better at capturing attention, humans must become better at protecting truth, meaning, compassion, and intention using technology as a tool without surrendering the distinctly human responsibility to witness, understand, and tell the stories that matter International journalist, news presenter, and analyst with 20 years of experience covering global affairs, conflict, and Southeast Europe. A former refugee from Bosnia, she combines lived experience with journalistic expertise to amplify voices from war-affected societies and explain complex political realities. She is
title: Who Tells the Human Story When Machines Control Attention? | Nafisa Latic | TEDxSarajevo

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores the difficult transition from elite sport to life beyond the court, and how identity, resilience, and purpose can be carried into a new chapter. Drawing on her own experience as a professional athlete forced to retire early after years of injuries, stress, and burnout, the speaker reflects on the pressure athletes face, the need for stronger mental-health support, and the challenge of rebuilding confidence after sport. She shows how skills developed through competition—focus, teamwork, adaptability, resilience, communication, and leadership—can become powerful assets in business and life, arguing that transition is not about losing who you were, but learning how to carry your strengths into a new arena. Former professional volleyball player and international sports professional with 12 years of experience across Europe and Asia, including a European Championship title and participation at the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games. Today, she works at the intersection of sport,
title: Singularity in transition | Sanja Malagurski | TEDxSarajevo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
AI can move faster than you. But it can't choose better than you - not yet. What are you actually chasing, and is it worth it? In this talk, Fareeha Amber Ansari explores what happens as AI takes on more of what we do. The qualities that make us distinctly human - judgment, trust, accountability, human connection - do not become less valuable.
They become our edge. Fareeha Amber Ansari is a two-time entrepreneur, data scientist, and AI educator. She has over 15 years working alongside leaders shaping how modern data and AI systems actually function in the messy reality of organizations. Amber has traveled to 29 countries, where she’s come to appreciate the vastness of human cultures and belief systems and how limited any single perspective will always be. Through her LinkedIn writing and as host of the podcast The Intelligent Human Enterprise, Amber is recognized as a trusted voice, bringing lived, often contrarian perspectives on how systems and human behavior influence one another.
title: Choose Your Chase: Staying Human in the AI Race | Fareeha Amber Ansari | TEDxManitou Springs Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it really mean to be a "good girl"? This talk explores how society conditions girls to prioritize obedience over authenticity, silence over self-expression, and approval over ambition. Through personal experiences and relatable stories, it challenges these invisible expectations and encourages individuals to redefine success on their own terms. "The Good Girl Myth" is a call to embrace confidence, use your voice, and live authentically without being limited by outdated stereotypes. Zohra Fakrudeen Ali, a fresher at Chennai Institute of Technology and a cybersecurity enthusiast interested in coding, ethical hacking, and sports.
Beyond technology, she questions how expectations placed on girls are defined, who defines them, and what they cost.

title: The Good Girl myth  | Zohra Fakrudeen Ali | TEDxChennai Institute of Technology Women
